findings.body:
**Let the unit-switch destroy command recover without `process.json`.**

The supplied `vm-unit-switch.py` destroy caller at Line 5089 uses the default `require_process=True`. If the host exits after QEMU starts but before it writes `process.json`, that caller fails in `load_run()` and never reaches the scope-ownership check. Pass `require_process=False` from that destroy caller, as this file does at Line 1609. Keep the identity requirement for callers that need it.
findings.title: Let the unit-switch destroy command recover without `process.json`.

findings.body:
**Require both manager-restart snapshots to have the same boot ID.**

If the guest reboots after the restart command returns but before the second `inspect`, the new boot can supply both a different manager PID and a different invocation ID. The report then accepts an isolated manager restart even though the observations span a guest reboot. A later planned reboot can still pass its own check.

Require nonempty, equal boot IDs in the manager snapshot pair. Keep the PID and invocation ID checks so an unchanged manager on the same boot does not pass.
findings.title: Require both manager-restart snapshots to have the same boot ID.

findings.body:
**Require a launch identity before caller-side failure cleanup.**

`cmd_run()` publishes `run.json` before it verifies source provenance or takes `run_lock`. If a separate `boot` starts that run and provenance verification then fails, `cmd_run()` calls `stop_owned_process(launched=None)` and stops the other invocation's VM. `cmd_boot()` can make the same unguarded call if `boot()` raises and a retry acquires the lock first.

Have `boot()` clean up partial launches under the lock. After it returns, let the CLI clean up only with the PID and start time of its own launch. A successful launch still has that identity for readiness-failure cleanup.






Also applies to: 1408-1410
findings.title: Require a launch identity before caller-side failure cleanup.

findings.body:
**Do not stop a scope that was absent during the ownership check.**

With the same run ID in two state directories, `destroy` in directory A can observe `LoadState=not-found`. Before A sends `stop`, `boot` in directory B can register the same scope under a different run lock. A then stops B's live VM without checking its members.

Do not send `stop` for an absent or empty scope. Give new launches a scope name tied to the canonical run directory. Keep the ownership check for a populated scope so an interrupted launch can still be recovered. Based on learnings, the scope name currently includes the run ID but not the state directory, so the name alone does not prove ownership.
findings.title: Do not stop a scope that was absent during the ownership check.

findings.body:
**Reject saved timing evidence without the required host load stamps.**

Remove `host_stamps` from an otherwise passing report and `verify` still exits 0. Recomputing the guest checks does not validate those stamps. Require the expected load stamps when `require_evidence=True`. Reports produced by `cmd_run()` already include them.
findings.title: Reject saved timing evidence without the required host load stamps.

findings.body:
**Keep partial-file cleanup warnings out of machine-mode stderr.**

If a download fails and `discard()` cannot unlink the partial file, it prints directly to stderr. `main()` then emits the JSON error, but its machine-mode guard cannot suppress the earlier warning. Attach the cleanup diagnostic to the primary exception and let the CLI serialize or narrate it. As per coding guidelines, in machine mode (`--json`) “stderr stays empty.”
findings.title: Keep partial-file cleanup warnings out of machine-mode stderr.

findings.body:
**Handle commas in state paths before building QEMU drive arguments.**

With a state directory named `probe,local`, preparation can create the overlay and seed, but QEMU interprets the comma in each `-drive` filename as an option delimiter. QEMU requires embedded commas to be doubled. Escape the path values used in QEMU options, or reject comma-containing state paths before preparation. ([qemu.org](https://www.qemu.org/docs/master/system/invocation.html?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Handle commas in state paths before building QEMU drive arguments.

findings.body:
**Protect the spawned process before writing the launch record.**

If `Recorder.append()` fails after `Popen()`, `boot()` skips its termination and wait logic. The caller can finish scope-based cleanup before `systemd-run` registers the scope. The pending child can then start QEMU after the CLI exits. In systemd v255, the scope launch registers the transient unit before it executes the command. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/v255/src/run/run.c))

Put the record write inside the cleanup block. If it fails, terminate and reap the child before releasing the run lock. Keep the record write on the successful path.
findings.title: Protect the spawned process before writing the launch record.

findings.body:
**Bind host provenance to the bytes that Python executes.**

`host_source.read_bytes()` reads the file after the program has started and prepared the image. If a locally modified host script starts and the checkout is restored during preparation, the commit comparison and retained artifact both see clean bytes. The running program still uses the modified code, but the report attributes its output to the clean commit.

Use a launcher that reads and verifies one host byte buffer before execution. Execute and retain that same buffer. The guest path already passes its verified byte buffer to the upload step.
findings.title: Bind host provenance to the bytes that Python executes.

findings.body:
**Bind each drain phase to its named seed.**

At Line 2871, `drain-alive --seed ambiguous` runs the ambiguous probe. If that probe succeeds, the driver writes its evidence to `drain-alive.json`. Derive the seed from the phase name, or reject a conflicting `--seed` as a usage error before dispatch.
findings.title: Bind each drain phase to its named seed.

findings.body:
**Verify two distinct switch-back completions against the fixture log.**

At Line 2626, two copies of the same completion pass if their sequence is newer than the baseline. If the fixture ran only once, the CLI can return two copies of that entry and the phase can still succeed. Make `validate_completed()` accept the expected unit and apply it to the retained repair record and post-switch log. Require distinct invocations, increasing sequences, and two matching successful Python entries.
findings.title: Verify two distinct switch-back completions against the fixture log.

findings.body:
**Reap the paused switch if the observation callback fails.**

If `show()` raises during the callback at Line 2138, `cli_paused()` skips both marker cleanup and child collection. The caller also skips its cleanup, so the phase exits while the paused child and marker are still outstanding. On callback failure, terminate and reap the child before removing the marker. On success, keep removing the marker to release the switch normally.
findings.title: Reap the paused switch if the observation callback fails.

findings.body:
**Require the same waiting start job after mask and reload.**

At Line 2562, a substring match accepts any row for `crq-repair.service`. If the seeded job `42` disappears and job `43` appears, the proof still passes this check. It can also accept a matching row from a failed `list-jobs` call. Require a successful observation and compare the exact unit, job ID, `start` operation, and `waiting` state with the seed captured at Line 2422.
findings.title: Require the same waiting start job after mask and reload.

findings.body:
**Do not count a zombie as a surviving fixture process.**

At Line 165, a successful `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` read sets `alive=True` even if the read is empty. Linux returns an empty command line for a zombie. If a switch kills a seeded child before the harness reaps it, the drain proof can still see `alive=True` and the original start time, then report that the child survived. ([man7.org](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_cmdline.5.html?utm_source=openai))

Read process state and start time from the same `/proc/<pid>/stat` sample. Reject zombie or dead states before setting `alive=True`. Keep reaping owned children during cleanup even if they have already exited. ([docs.python.org](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html?highlight=process&utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Do not count a zombie as a surviving fixture process.

findings.body:
**Ignore a trailing unterminated line in the completion reader.**

`read_completions` parses the final line of the log even when a writer has not yet appended its newline. The fixture writers append one complete, newline-terminated record per run, but the reader does not wait for the newline. During an append, the reader can therefore see a partial line and raise `RuntimeError`. `wait_completion` does not catch that error, so the path positive control fails even though the fixture is still writing. Parse only newline-terminated lines:

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-    for number, line in enumerate(path.read_text().splitlines(), 1):
+    text = path.read_text()
+    # A writer may be mid-append. Only newline-terminated records are complete.
+    lines = text.split("\n")[:-1]
+    for number, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
```

</details>
findings.title: Ignore a trailing unterminated line in the completion reader.
